entities.name: William M. Meredith
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
William Morris Meredith (1799–1873) was an American Whig politician and lawyer from Pennsylvania who served as Secretary of the Treasury under President Zachary Taylor (1849–1850) and as a prominent Pennsylvania Whig leader. His Treasury tenure was brief — Taylor's sudden death in July 1850 ended the administration — but it coincided with the most intense debate over the Compromise of 1850 and the California statehood question. Meredith was a Philadelphia lawyer and one of the most distinguished members of the Pennsylvania bar.

After his Treasury service he continued as a leading Pennsylvania lawyer and was state Attorney General (1861–1867) during the Civil War — managing Pennsylvania's legal affairs during the war.

He was the founding president of the Union League of Philadelphia.

He was one of Philadelphia's most eminent antebellum lawyers and civic leaders.
